open_obligations.what_is_open: For fixed \(0<c<1\) in the two residual regions, the available achievability and converse exponents do not coincide in general. It remains unknown whether an exact exponent \(\rho(\alpha,\beta,s,d)\) exists at every residual tuple, what its value is when it exists, and on which nontrivial residual subregions it is independent of \(\beta\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Lemma~\texttt{lem:optimized-deficient-rate-bracket} supplies the explicit upper-risk exponent \(R_{\mathrm{ach}}=\max\{R_{\mathrm{sep}},R_{\mathrm{hist}}\}\), while Lemma~\texttt{lem:extreme-low-s-fuzzy-lower} supplies only the combined converse exponent \(r_{\mathrm{low}}=\min\{2\alpha/(2\alpha+1),8/[4+2/(\alpha\vee\beta)+d/s]\}\). These exponents need not agree. Lemma~\texttt{lem:population-piecewise-polynomial-projection} gives the population projection bias and rank identities needed by a higher-order route, but it does not construct a uniformly stable empirical projection under an arbitrary Borel covariate density. Lemma~\texttt{lem:prescribed-low-s-projection-rank-obstruction} further shows that the prescribed full-rank empirical Gram inverse is necessarily singular when \(s<\alpha d/\{4(\alpha+1)\}\); stabilized alternatives are not ruled out, but no matching risk analysis for one follows from the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: The separated-pilot and histogram/local-polynomial estimators were optimized to obtain \(R_{\mathrm{ach}}\); a fuzzy two-prior construction was optimized to obtain the low-\(s\) converse; and a piecewise-polynomial higher-order projection route was examined. The last route yields a \(k^{-2s/d}\) population remainder and a rank-\(k\) kernel second moment, but the proposed empirical Gram inverse fails by dimension counting in the extreme-low-\(s\) subregion and does not close the remaining band without a new stabilization argument and a matching converse.
